key_findings.finding_1_no_mean_improvement: Physics features produce no statistically significant improvement in mean performance across any of the three splits. ΔR² in [-0.0001, +0.0009], well within seed standard error.
key_findings.finding_2_variance_increases_under_shift: On S3 (high-pressure extrapolation), seed variance INCREASED from σ_R²=0.009 (baseline) to 0.020 (with physics). Variance amplification factor: 10.3× → 25.4×.
key_findings.finding_3_explanation: Hypothesized cause: non-dimensional groups (especially density ratio) depend strongly nonlinearly on P near the water critical point (~22.06 MPa), amplifying sensitivity to which test points fall in the extrapolation regime.

paper_implications.reframe: Physics ablation strengthens the variance amplification narrative: the phenomenon is architectural, not feature-related. Physics-aware feature engineering CANNOT cure it.
paper_implications.discussion_section: Section 5.1 update — variance amplification is architectural
paper_implications.table_5_update: Add columns for Physics features and Hybrid priors

positioning_against_reviewer_critique: Reviewer would ask: "Did you test physics-aware features?" Answer: Yes, we tested 3 non-dimensional groups; they do not improve XGBoost on this benchmark and may even worsen variance under extrapolation. This negative result is publishable and reinforces our central thesis.
